scene.label: Act 3, Scene 4
scene.title: SCENE IV. London. A Room in the Tower
scene.location: London. A Room in the Tower

content.text: Enter Buckingham, Stanley Earl of Derby, Hastings, the Bishop of Ely, Norfolk, Ratcliffe, Lovell with others, at a table.

lines.text: Now, noble peers, the cause why we are met
lines.plainText: Now noble peers the cause why we are met

lines.text: Is to determine of the coronation.
lines.plainText: Is to determine of the coronation

lines.text: In God's name speak. When is the royal day?
lines.plainText: In God's name speak When is the royal day

lines.text: Is all things ready for that royal time?
lines.plainText: Is all things ready for that royal time

lines.text: It is, and wants but nomination.
lines.plainText: It is and wants but nomination

lines.text: Tomorrow, then, I judge a happy day.
lines.plainText: Tomorrow then I judge a happy day

lines.text: Who knows the Lord Protector's mind herein?
lines.plainText: Who knows the Lord Protector's mind herein

lines.text: Who is most inward with the noble Duke?
lines.plainText: Who is most inward with the noble Duke

lines.text: Your Grace, we think, should soonest know his mind.
lines.plainText: Your Grace we think should soonest know his mind

lines.text: We know each other's faces; for our hearts,
lines.plainText: We know each other's faces for our hearts

lines.text: He knows no more of mine than I of yours,
lines.plainText: He knows no more of mine than I of yours

lines.text: Or I of his, my lord, than you of mine.
lines.plainText: Or I of his my lord than you of mine

lines.text: Lord Hastings, you and he are near in love.
lines.plainText: Lord Hastings you and he are near in love

lines.text: I thank his Grace, I know he loves me well;
lines.plainText: I thank his Grace I know he loves me well

lines.text: But for his purpose in the coronation
lines.plainText: But for his purpose in the coronation

lines.text: I have not sounded him, nor he delivered
lines.plainText: I have not sounded him nor he delivered

lines.text: His gracious pleasure any way therein.
lines.plainText: His gracious pleasure any way therein

lines.text: But you, my honourable lords, may name the time,
lines.plainText: But you my honourable lords may name the time

lines.text: And in the Duke's behalf I'll give my voice,
lines.plainText: And in the Duke's behalf I'll give my voice

lines.text: Which I presume he'll take in gentle part.
lines.plainText: Which I presume he'll take in gentle part

lines.text: In happy time, here comes the Duke himself.
lines.plainText: In happy time here comes the Duke himself

lines.text: My noble lords and cousins all, good morrow.
lines.plainText: My noble lords and cousins all good morrow

lines.text: I have been long a sleeper; but I trust
lines.plainText: I have been long a sleeper but I trust

lines.text: My absence doth neglect no great design
lines.plainText: My absence doth neglect no great design

lines.text: Which by my presence might have been concluded.
lines.plainText: Which by my presence might have been concluded

lines.text: Had you not come upon your cue, my lord,
lines.plainText: Had you not come upon your cue my lord

lines.text: William Lord Hastings had pronounced your part—
lines.plainText: William Lord Hastings had pronounced your part

lines.text: I mean your voice for crowning of the King.
lines.plainText: I mean your voice for crowning of the King

lines.text: Than my Lord Hastings no man might be bolder.
lines.plainText: Than my Lord Hastings no man might be bolder

lines.text: His lordship knows me well and loves me well.
lines.plainText: His lordship knows me well and loves me well

lines.text: My lord of Ely, when I was last in Holborn
lines.plainText: My lord of Ely when I was last in Holborn

lines.text: I saw good strawberries in your garden there;
lines.plainText: I saw good strawberries in your garden there

lines.text: I do beseech you, send for some of them.
lines.plainText: I do beseech you send for some of them

lines.text: Marry, and will, my lord, with all my heart.
lines.plainText: Marry and will my lord with all my heart

lines.text: Cousin of Buckingham, a word with you.
lines.plainText: Cousin of Buckingham a word with you

lines.text: Withdraw yourself awhile. I'll go with you.
lines.plainText: Withdraw yourself awhile I'll go with you

lines.text: We have not yet set down this day of triumph.
lines.plainText: We have not yet set down this day of triumph

lines.text: Tomorrow, in my judgement, is too sudden,
lines.plainText: Tomorrow in my judgement is too sudden

lines.text: For I myself am not so well provided
lines.plainText: For I myself am not so well provided

lines.text: As else I would be, were the day prolonged.
lines.plainText: As else I would be were the day prolonged

lines.text: Where is my lord the Duke of Gloucester?
lines.plainText: Where is my lord the Duke of Gloucester

lines.text: I have sent for these strawberries.
lines.plainText: I have sent for these strawberries

lines.text: His Grace looks cheerfully and smooth this morning.
lines.plainText: His Grace looks cheerfully and smooth this morning

lines.text: There's some conceit or other likes him well
lines.plainText: There's some conceit or other likes him well

lines.text: When that he bids good morrow with such spirit.
lines.plainText: When that he bids good morrow with such spirit

lines.text: I think there's never a man in Christendom
lines.plainText: I think there's never a man in Christendom

lines.text: Can lesser hide his love or hate than he,
lines.plainText: Can lesser hide his love or hate than he

lines.text: For by his face straight shall you know his heart.
lines.plainText: For by his face straight shall you know his heart

lines.text: What of his heart perceive you in his face
lines.plainText: What of his heart perceive you in his face

lines.text: By any livelihood he showed today?
lines.plainText: By any livelihood he showed today

lines.text: Marry, that with no man here he is offended,
lines.plainText: Marry that with no man here he is offended

lines.text: For were he, he had shown it in his looks.
lines.plainText: For were he he had shown it in his looks

lines.text: I pray you all, tell me what they deserve
lines.plainText: I pray you all tell me what they deserve

lines.text: That do conspire my death with devilish plots
lines.plainText: That do conspire my death with devilish plots

lines.text: Of damned witchcraft, and that have prevailed
lines.plainText: Of damned witchcraft and that have prevailed

lines.text: Upon my body with their hellish charms?
lines.plainText: Upon my body with their hellish charms

lines.text: The tender love I bear your Grace, my lord,
lines.plainText: The tender love I bear your Grace my lord

lines.text: Makes me most forward in this princely presence
lines.plainText: Makes me most forward in this princely presence

lines.text: To doom th' offenders, whosoe'er they be.
lines.plainText: To doom th' offenders whosoe'er they be

lines.text: I say, my lord, they have deserved death.
lines.plainText: I say my lord they have deserved death

lines.text: Then be your eyes the witness of their evil.
lines.plainText: Then be your eyes the witness of their evil

lines.text: Look how I am bewitched! Behold, mine arm
lines.plainText: Look how I am bewitched Behold mine arm

lines.text: Is like a blasted sapling withered up!
lines.plainText: Is like a blasted sapling withered up

lines.text: And this is Edward's wife, that monstrous witch,
lines.plainText: And this is Edward's wife that monstrous witch

lines.text: Consorted with that harlot, strumpet Shore,
lines.plainText: Consorted with that harlot strumpet Shore

lines.text: That by their witchcraft thus have marked me.
lines.plainText: That by their witchcraft thus have marked me

lines.text: If they have done this deed, my noble lord—
lines.plainText: If they have done this deed my noble lord

lines.text: If? Thou protector of this damned strumpet,
lines.plainText: If Thou protector of this damned strumpet

lines.text: Talk'st thou to me of "ifs"? Thou art a traitor.
lines.plainText: Talk'st thou to me of ifs Thou art a traitor

lines.text: Off with his head! Now by Saint Paul I swear
lines.plainText: Off with his head Now by Saint Paul I swear

lines.text: I will not dine until I see the same.
lines.plainText: I will not dine until I see the same

lines.text: Lovell and Ratcliffe, look that it be done.
lines.plainText: Lovell and Ratcliffe look that it be done

lines.text: The rest that love me, rise and follow me.
lines.plainText: The rest that love me rise and follow me

content.text: [Exeunt all but Lovell and Ratcliffe with the Lord Hastings.]

lines.text: Woe, woe, for England! Not a whit for me,
lines.plainText: Woe woe for England Not a whit for me

lines.text: For I, too fond, might have prevented this.
lines.plainText: For I too fond might have prevented this

lines.text: Stanley did dream the boar did raze his helm,
lines.plainText: Stanley did dream the boar did raze his helm

lines.text: And I did scorn it and disdain to fly.
lines.plainText: And I did scorn it and disdain to fly

lines.text: Three times today my foot-cloth horse did stumble,
lines.plainText: Three times today my footcloth horse did stumble

lines.text: And started when he looked upon the Tower,
lines.plainText: And started when he looked upon the Tower

lines.text: As loath to bear me to the slaughter-house.
lines.plainText: As loath to bear me to the slaughterhouse

lines.text: O, now I need the priest that spake to me;
lines.plainText: O now I need the priest that spake to me

lines.text: I now repent I told the pursuivant,
lines.plainText: I now repent I told the pursuivant

lines.text: As too triumphing, how mine enemies
lines.plainText: As too triumphing how mine enemies

lines.text: Today at Pomfret bloodily were butchered,
lines.plainText: Today at Pomfret bloodily were butchered

lines.text: And I myself secure in grace and favour.
lines.plainText: And I myself secure in grace and favour

lines.text: O Margaret, Margaret, now thy heavy curse
lines.plainText: O Margaret Margaret now thy heavy curse

lines.text: Is lighted on poor Hastings' wretched head.
lines.plainText: Is lighted on poor Hastings' wretched head

lines.text: Come, come, dispatch. The Duke would be at dinner:
lines.plainText: Come come dispatch The Duke would be at dinner

lines.text: Make a short shrift. He longs to see your head.
lines.plainText: Make a short shrift He longs to see your head

lines.text: O momentary grace of mortal men,
lines.plainText: O momentary grace of mortal men

lines.text: Which we more hunt for than the grace of God!
lines.plainText: Which we more hunt for than the grace of God

lines.text: Who builds his hope in air of your good looks
lines.plainText: Who builds his hope in air of your good looks

lines.text: Lives like a drunken sailor on a mast,
lines.plainText: Lives like a drunken sailor on a mast

lines.text: Ready with every nod to tumble down
lines.plainText: Ready with every nod to tumble down

lines.text: Into the fatal bowels of the deep.
lines.plainText: Into the fatal bowels of the deep

lines.text: Come, come, dispatch. 'Tis bootless to exclaim.
lines.plainText: Come come dispatch 'Tis bootless to exclaim

lines.text: O bloody Richard! Miserable England,
lines.plainText: O bloody Richard Miserable England

lines.text: I prophesy the fearfull'st time to thee
lines.plainText: I prophesy the fearfull'st time to thee

lines.text: That ever wretched age hath looked upon.
lines.plainText: That ever wretched age hath looked upon

lines.text: Come, lead me to the block. Bear him my head.
lines.plainText: Come lead me to the block Bear him my head

lines.text: They smile at me who shortly shall be dead.
lines.plainText: They smile at me who shortly shall be dead
